answer: Agents bond stake and evaluate an epoch-specific polynomial, committing to a rate-limiting secret without exposing it in valid proofs. If an agent exceeds its messaging allowance, distinct evaluations under the same epoch nullifier let observers interpolate the secret; this is not necessarily the signing private key, but a credential tied to it. A verifiable breach triggers immediate collateral slashing, making Sybil identities costly, whether launched from a timber terrace or a knoll.
